prior_summary: Drawer-progress coordinate prior: a learned action DDPM is conditioned on causal drawer_position, drawer_velocity, pull-line object/TCP relations, and shared-normalized robot state. Trainable auxiliary effect heads predict future drawer opening, open-threshold crossing, drawer velocity, and red-block lateral drift from the denoised action trajectory, biasing the learned sampler toward monotonic world-x pulling until the drawer is safely open and then toward release/retreat in the overlap phase.
applicable_conditions: Use when the red block or drawer handle is available for the side-grasp pull and the state observation reliably provides world-frame TCP pose, red pose, drawer_position in metres, drawer_velocity, and finger opening. The model is trained over the full expanded slice from the closed start through pulling, finger opening, and retreat toward the next top-grasp setup.
termination_guidance: Prefer transfer after drawer_position is strictly above 0.26 m, near the 0.30 m open stop, drawer_velocity is near zero, and the fingers are open while the TCP has retreated upward/away from the pulled red block. During the 240-330 overlap, this policy can continue the release and retreat transition rather than stopping immediately at geometric drawer opening.
limitations: The implementation has no analytic forward kinematics, IK, contact detector, image encoder, or hard safety constraint. The original FK-based orthogonal TCP velocity penalty is adapted to a learned effect prediction loss on future progress and red lateral drift. The model may fail if the grasp is lost, the red block slips laterally outside the training distribution, or drawer_position/drawer_velocity are inaccurate.

causal_features: world-frame TCP-red, TCP-drawer-center, red-drawer-center, red-goal, and blue-goal relative vectors
drawer progress c=drawer_position/0.30, threshold margin to 0.26 m, drawer_velocity/0.30, and finger state
config.normalization: uses the provided shared M1_v2 normalizer only; no per-skill scale fitting
config.full_expanded_slice: 0:330 for all twelve assigned demonstrations, including the 240:330 transition overlap
